sections.overview: Scoliopteryx libatrix, the Herald, is an Erebidae moth whose adults overwinter.
sections.identification: Its orange-brown wings have pale markings and a scalloped outer edge.
sections.habitat: Larvae use willows (Salix) and poplars (Populus), while adults shelter in caves, cellars and other sheltered places.
sections.diet: Caterpillars feed on willow and poplar foliage.
sections.behavior: Adults overwinter, often in caves or buildings, and may be seen on the wing in both autumn and spring.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs on willows and poplars; the caterpillars later pupate between leaves joined with silk.
sections.ecology: Its life cycle links damp, often wooded settings with sheltered winter roosts.
sections.conservation: The regional and species accounts consulted describe its biology and distribution but provide no global conservation assessment.
